name: Slip-Lock Bypass: Nonlocal F+ with Independent Stiff-Vector Frame and Decoupled Kinetic
claimed_mechanism: Bypasses the slip-lock theorem (DC-013) by introducing a genuine preferred-frame stiff vector whose longitudinal mode mediates the lensing correction off the delta-R ray. The nonlocal F+ operator provides the MOND force law globally, while the stiff vector provides the required off-ray coupling locally. The stiff vector's kinetic normalization is fixed by an independent bare mass, decoupling the PPN response from the kinetic term (resolving P7).
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the nonlocal F+ term yields the MOND acceleration. The stiff vector's longitudinal mode contributes to the spatial metric perturbation (Psi) but not to the temporal metric (Phi), yielding the required lensing enhancement without slipping into the f(R) ray. The PPN parameters alpha_1 and alpha_2 are suppressed by e^-y in the high-acceleration limit, satisfying the Solar System constraints.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-012 (frameless localized-nonlocal) because it explicitly includes a preferred-frame vector, which is the necessary escape from the slip-lock. It is inequivalent to DC-010 (khronometric) because it uses a standard kinetic stiff vector with an independent bare mass, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall where the screening coefficient also controls the kinetic normalization. It is inequivalent to FM-000004 because the stiff vector's kinetic term is decoupled from the nonlocal MOND kernel, preventing the longitudinal mode from becoming strongly coupled in the screened regime.
